The UNFPA Strategic Plan for 2026-2029 articulates the organization’s response to a complex global environment, providing a roadmap for resilience and renewal. It is designed to accelerate the implementation of the Programme of Action of the International Conference on Population and Development (ICPD) and the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals by 2030. This mandate is pursued through a focus on four interconnected outcomes: ending the unmet need for family planning; ending preventable maternal deaths; ending gender-based violence and harmful practices; and adapting to demographic change through evidence and rights-based policies. In a world where fundamental human rights are at risk, we need principled and ethical staff who embody these international norms and standards and will defend them courageously and with full conviction. UNFPA is seeking candidates who transform, inspire, and deliver high-impact sustained results, ensuring effective external relations, communications, partnership-building and resource mobilization in a rapidly changing development and funding landscape. We need staff who are transparent, exceptional in how they manage the resources entrusted to them, and who commit to delivering excellence in programme results Job Purpose The UNFPA Togo Country Office is implementing its Eighth Country Programme, which runs until December 2027, while preparing for the Ninth Country Programme, beginning in January 2028. Maintain accurate records and documentation of partnership commitments, opportunities, and follow-up actions. Initiating, tracking, and consolidating inputs to ensure the timely preparation, quality assurance, and submission of donor reports. Coordinating inputs from Programme, M&E, Finance, and Operations teams to ensure consistency between technical achievements, narrative descriptions, and financial data. Gathering and documenting lessons learned, best practices, case studies, and programme results for resource mobilization and advocacy tools. Assisting Programme teams with analytical writing, reporting templates, and donor-specific compliance requirements. Coordinate the Preparation of analytical notes on opportunities, risks, and trends to assist management in strategic decision-making. Support UNFPA's participation in technical working groups, national forums, and coordination mechanisms by preparing background documents. Contribute technical content to advocacy and communication materials highlighting UNFPA's contributions to national priorities and the SDGs. PROGRAMME PLANNING, COORDINATION AND KNOWLEDGE MANAGEMENT The Incumbent Will Work closely with Programme teams to identify sub-programme priorities requiring funding and partnership support. Provide technical inputs to programme reviews, planning exercises, and internal coordination meetings. Draft and update internal tools, templates, and guidance materials to improve reporting efficiency and proposal quality. Act as CO focal point for Humanitarian response funds mobilization and management. Key Outcomes Increased & Diversified Funding Portfolio Outcome: Mobilization of new financial resources and successful diversification of funding streams beyond traditional sources. Impact: Secures long-term financial sustainability for the Country Office and helps scale up both regular and humanitarian programming (particularly in response to the crisis in the Savanes Region). High-Quality Donor Reporting & Full Project Compliance Outcome: Timely delivery of accurate, high-impact, results-based progress reports across all donor projects, with direct management of the EUR 7.5 million Luxembourg portfolio. Impact: Builds institutional credibility, protects donor trust, and ensures strict adherence to donor agreements over the multi-year implementation period. Strengthened Strategic Partnerships & Institutional Capacity Outcome: Enhanced strategic positioning of UNFPA in Togo, established co-financing partnerships, and upgraded internal capacity of staff and partners in proposal writing and donor management. Impact: Position UNFPA as a partner of choice in Togolese health and development initiatives, preparing the Country Office for a smooth transition into its Ninth Country Programme (2028–2032). Qualifications And Experience The successful candidate should have a master’s degree in international development, Social Sciences, International Relations, Public Administration, Business Administration, Communications or another relevant field. The candidate should have at least five years of progressively responsible professional experience in projects management, resource mobilization, donor relations, strategic partnerships and donor reporting in an international development environment. Challenge sequencing, productivity assumptions and resource allocation to improve programme certainty. Produce clear progress reports, forecasts and presentations for senior management, the client and the consultant. Advanced Primavera P6 skills and a thorough understanding of critical path analysis, resource loading, progress measurement and forecasting.
